title: Canonical tensor-Hom adjunction formula for an immersion
statement:
Let $A$ be a finite commutative ring and let $s:S\hookrightarrow X$ be an immersion with a chosen factorization $S\xrightarrow{i}U\xrightarrow{j}X$, where $i$ is closed and $j$ is open [def-weil-closed-immersion, def-weil-open-immersion]. Put $Rs_!=j_!i_*$, $Rs^!=Ri^!j^*$ and let $Rs_*$ denote ordinary derived direct image; $j_!$ is exact extension by zero [lem-cbc-open-closed-recollement], and $Ri^!$ is the ambient right adjoint of $i_*$ [lem-exc-closed-ambient]. Use ordinary unbounded derived categories $D(T_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ of sheaves of modules over the constant ring sheaf $A_T$ on small etale sites [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories], derived tensor $\otimes_A^L$ [def-kun-derived-tensor], and derived internal Hom $\mathscr H_T(U,V)=R\mathcal Hom_{A_T}(U,V)$ [def-pur-derived-internal-hom]. Scheme inverse images on these categories are exact constant-coefficient inverse images [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact]. For $P\in D(S_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ and $M\in D(X_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ put $H=\mathscr H_S(P,Rs^!M)$. There is a natural isomorphism
$$\theta_{s,P,M}:\mathscr H_X(Rs_!P,M)\xrightarrow{\sim}Rs_*H$$
characterized as follows. For every $C\in D(X_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ and $u:C\to Rs_*H$, let $\widetilde u:s^*C\to H$ be its adjoint under $s^*\dashv Rs_*$. The tensor-adjoint of $\theta_{s,P,M}^{-1}\circ u$ is exactly
$$C\otimes_A^LRs_!P\xrightarrow{\pi_s}Rs_!(s^*C\otimes_A^LP)\xrightarrow{Rs_!(\widetilde u\otimes1)}Rs_!(H\otimes_A^LP)\xrightarrow{Rs_!\mathrm{ev}}Rs_!Rs^!M\xrightarrow{\varepsilon^!_{s,M}}M.$$
Here $\pi_s$ is the canonical projection isomorphism [lem-sf-etale-generic-immersion-projection] and $\varepsilon^!$ is the counit of $Rs_!\dashv Rs^!$. No boundedness or constructibility of $C,P,M$ is required.

proof.text: Reuse the canonical derived adjunction derivedUpperStarLowerStarAdjunction for L(s^*) left adjoint to R(s_*), and the existing derivedOpenImmersionLowerShriekUpperStarAdjunction for exact open extension by zero. Compose the latter with the closed-ambient adjunction of lem-exc-closed-ambient to obtain the specified immersionLowerUpperShriekAdjunction, with exactly its given counit. These upstream derived interfaces already implement the exact inverse-image and extension-by-zero adjunctions; no new K-injective reconstruction is necessary in this module.

Use the existing closed derived internal Hom derivedHom and its parametrized adjunction derivedTensorHomAdjunction₂. Transport this adjunction along the canonical derivedTensorSymmetry to right-ordered tensor, so that its inverse Hom equivalence sends f to (f tensor identity), signed symmetry, then the original counit; naturality of symmetry proves this formula. This is precisely immersionHomEvaluation. The source derived tensor/internal-Hom interfaces already provide this structure, so the separate general ringed-site existence theorem is not needed.

The isomorphism and two-variable naturality clauses of immersionProjectionFormula assemble into an isomorphism of left-adjoint bifunctors, from (P,C) mapped to C tensor Rs_! P to (P,C) mapped to Rs_!(s^* C tensor P). Compose the right-ordered tensor-Hom parametrized adjunction on S with s^* left adjoint to Rs_* and Rs_! left adjoint to Rs^!. Compare it with the right-ordered tensor-Hom adjunction on X precomposed in the parameter by Rs_!. ParametrizedAdjunction.conjugateIso, followed by objectwise uncurrying, gives the required natural isomorphism theta. The uncurrying naturality equation uses only functoriality of Rs_*.

Apply the elementary conjugate-equivalence counit identity to the projection transformation. Expanding the inverse Hom equivalence of the composed adjunction gives the inverse of s^* left adjoint to Rs_*, then the right-ordered tensor-Hom inverse on S, then the inverse of Rs_! left adjoint to Rs^!. The symmetry calculation of step 2 identifies both tensor-Hom inverses with tensoring the input map by the identity followed by immersionHomEvaluation. Functoriality distributes Rs_! over that composite, producing exactly projection, Rs_! of the adjoint map tensor identity, Rs_! evaluation, and the specified exceptional counit, as claimed. No boundedness or constructibility is used.
